title: Alexander H. Everett to Henry Clay, Madrid, 25 Sep 1825: the six coded passages of the Notes of a conversation with Mr Zea, in the State Department code (catalogue 638)

documents.shelfmark: NARA RG 59, Despatches from US Ministers to Spain vol. 25, M31 reel 27 (naId 188610348), frames 0112-0115 (MS pp. 1-6) and 0119-0121 (MS pp. 14-15, 17-18), enclosure 'Notes of a Conversation of Mr. Everett with Mr. Zea' (catalogue 638, which counted frames 0119-0121 only)

plaintext.source: The State Department's period decipherment of all six coded parts of the Notes, M31 roll 27 frames 0110 (right page, parts 1-4) and 0111 (parts 4-6), writer and date unknown; found by Andrew Beling on 22 Nov 2026, transcribed in beling/period_decipherment.txt by one AI reader with no second reader. Manning III (1925) doc. 1134 p. 2062 prints passage A as '[Here follow six lines in cipher, without decodification.]'; passages B and C are not printed.

transcription.notes: Collated on 24 Nov 2026 (we028.py) from three transcriptions made independently with AI models: WAINUT's passages A, B, C (355 groups, 27 Oct 2026), Brice Dudout's eight pages (1,117 groups in his files) and Andrew Beling's six sections (1,201 groups). corrections = the six groups of Dudout's files changed in the collated file (628, 458, 845, 1081, 1564, 880); a code line missing from his p. 18 files is restored from the other two. Two groups keep a doubt mark (1057?, 1383?). Measured with docs/_check_profile.py --measure --digits --drop-first: 1,201 groups, 474 different with their marks (444 different numbers). The first document count, 355 groups, was passages A to C only (everett1825_transcription.txt).

system.summary: The State Department's numerical code of 1,600 numbers for words, syllables and letters (the = 1385), whose sheet survives at NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057 (Weber's WE028); the code of John Quincy Adams's despatches of 1811-1812, rebuilt in ../jqa before the sheet was known here.

diacritics.note: marks under and after a group, by rules printed on the sheet: a cross under a figure doubles a letter, a tick withdraws one (two or three ticks, two or three letters), a lozenge makes a noun plural or genitive and a verb third person, a caret makes a participle or past tense

system.sibling_key: the State Department code sheet as transcribed in ../morris1813/beling/key/codebook_M97_13_transcription.csv, applied on 24 Nov 2026 (key_we028_everett1825.tsv); the first readings of 27 Oct 2026 used the table rebuilt from the same code in ../jqa/code_table.tsv, unchanged
system.notes: distinct_symbols = different groups in everett1825_collated_transcription.txt with their marks (python docs/_check_profile.py --measure --digits --drop-first); 444 different numbers. nomenclator.entries is the size of the sheet. unread_groups = 1: 1601, which is not a number of the sheet (read as a slip for 1001). word_division none: the groups run on, sentence ends are marked by a dash or a stroke.

prior_solution.where: The State Department's decipherment of the time of all six coded parts, M31 roll 27 frames 0110-0111, just before the Notes on the same reel; found on 22 Nov 2026 by Andrew Beling, after the two first readings here (27 Oct 2026) were made. It is the first decipherment of all six parts. No word of the reading of record was taken from it: every word counted as read is given by the code sheet; it was one of the grounds for choosing between transcriptions at nine places (628, 458, 845, 1081, 1564, 880, 1057?/1257, 1383?/1388 and 1385/1345 at 114R.03.6, where the film check went against Dudout's files or was split), and it is quoted beside each hole. The part split of 23 Nov 2026 (pp. 1-6 read from existing decipherment) was decided before the code sheet was applied and was withdrawn on 24 Nov 2026: with the sheet both parts are read with the known key. Earlier record: Manning III (1925) doc. 1134 p. 2062 prints passage A as '[Here follow six lines in cipher, without decodification.]' and omits B and C; one web search found no decipherment. Not checked: another copy of the Notes, a separate State Department file, the Clay Papers. A pencil note 'Decyphered' stands at the foot of MS p. 4 (frame 0114). Brice Dudout's parallel reading of all the cipher was published the same day as WAINUT's (Europe chiffrée, 27 Oct 2026); neither used the other.

solution.what: WAINUT contribution: located catalogue 638 on NARA M31 reel 27 frames 0119-0121 (Everett, Madrid, 25 Sep 1825), in the JQA code (the = 1385).
WAINUT contribution: 355 groups in three passages (A 8 lines, B 14, C 12), checked line by line against the frames a second time, independently.
WAINUT contribution: applied ../jqa/code_table.tsv unchanged: 347 of 355 groups valued, running English in all three passages.
WAINUT contribution: context values marked [?] (666 Zea against March, 70, 1072, and 17 context words); 8 groups open.

WAINUT contribution: wrong-key controls (decode.py --controls): function-word rate 0.37 for the true table, 0.02-0.12 for shifts of 1-100, 0.03-0.05 for random table permutations; an independent character-trigram check (Manning-trained) put the true order at -2.129 against shuffled orders best -2.351.
WAINUT contribution: Manning III doc. 1134 (p. 2062) is an extract that prints passage A undecoded, without passages B and C; one web search found no decipherment.
WAINUT contribution: read in part (everett1825_reading.md, read_share 0.904): 23 holes in about 240 words.

Review check of frames 0112-0118 (catalogue counts from 0114): the same Notes, endorsed as the duplicate sent with despatch No. 7 of 25 Sept 1825, carry further coded passages on MS pp. 1-6 (frames 0112-0115: short runs on pp. 1-3, pp. 4-5 wholly in code, nine lines on p. 6; about 80 lines, very roughly 900 groups); pp. 7-13 are clear. A pencil 'Decyphered' stands at the foot of p. 4. Not transcribed.

Brice Dudout's parallel, independent reading published (https://bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/documents.html#everett-1825): same table frozen, checked first on the despatch of 8 Sept 1825 against Manning doc. 1133 (288/304 = 0.947, permuted p99 0.023); six lines 72 of 74 groups; pp. 1-6 and 17-18, 1,111 of 1,127 (0.986), with an Everett overlay (727 rather, 1201 g, 557 thro, 948 Russia; ../jqa/overlay_dudout.tsv). Passage A agrees ("a language imposed upon him at present by particular circumstances"); not compared group by group.

Reading review of the nine outcome.texts entries: WAINUT's three passages (everett1825_reading.md) and Brice Dudout's eight pages (dudout/texts/*_reading.md) read as sentences against their group-by-group decryptions; all coherent with scattered marked holes, grade A recorded on each. Word-level read_share measured on the deciphered passages of the eight pages (unresolved groups as holes): 1.0, 1.0, 0.969, 0.969, 0.988, 0.958, 0.991, 1.0; counting words given whole from sense as holes too, pp. 1, 2, 3 and 6 fall to 0.949, 0.917, 0.948, 0.944. The two readings of pp. 17-18 were not reconciled (WAINUT [?cause] / [125] against Dudout {measure} / {contrary}). Frames not re-opened.

Andrew Beling contribution (beling/): the State Department's period decipherment of all six coded parts found on M31 roll 27 frames 0110-0111 and transcribed; it settles 70 necessary ("ity" above) and 125 contrary. Three transcriptions compared group by group (with Dudout's files 1,113 in both, 1,086 agree, 27 differ; WAINUT's A 74/74, B-C 278/281); a code line missing from dudout/texts/p18 found. The 27 differing groups read blind by an AI model reader with no candidates given; the 11 it was unsure of went to a second blind reader that saw the whole line (crops, positions and readings in beling/film_check): Dudout's digit at 18, Beling's at 8, 1 undecided; ten control readings correct. Of the 8, 628 and 1564 rest on one model reader and 845 and 880 are ambiguous in the first digit (345 or 845, 380 or 880). The transcription of the period decipherment has one reader. No reading changed.

Integration of PR #900 (owner's decision of 23 Nov 2026): pp. 1-6 made their own part in outcome.parts, read from existing decipherment (the period decipherment on frames 0110-0111; the clerk's corrections of his own key values noted; its transcription has one AI reader and no second reader); pp. 14-18 stay read with known key. The not-attempted gap for pp. 1-6 removed. The 39 crops of beling/film_check/crops removed from the repository with the contributor's agreement; positions.tsv, readings.tsv (pixel boxes) and the frame links kept. The eight value edits to dudout/texts that the film check supports (628, 458, 845, 1081, 1564, 1257, 880, 1388) are listed in NOTES as proposed and not applied: 628 and 1564 rest on one model reader, 845 and 880 are ambiguous in the first digit, no person has looked. No reading file changed; no page re-measured; frames not opened in this pass.

The State Department code sheet (NARA M97 roll 13 frames 1056-1057, Weber's WE028; Andrew Beling's transcription in ../morris1813/beling/key) applied to every group of the six coded parts: a value for 443 of the 444 different numbers (not 1601, which is not on the sheet), among them the eight the JQA table lacked (125 contrary, 126 convey, 211 pret, 258 spi, 850 dispose, 917 os, 1354 br, 1512 acy). Four rows of the sheet transcription corrected: 233 sim, 234 sin and 1093 shal as the alphabetical sheet prints them (frame 1056 looked at), 681 are from its numerical half. key_we028_everett1825.tsv.

The sheet's printed instructions for the marks read on frame 1056 and transcribed in NOTES: a lozenge makes a noun genitive or plural and a verb third person, a caret a participle or imperfect, a cross under a figure doubles the corresponding letter, a tick under a figure withdraws it; u and v, i and j are convertible. Every marked group of the six parts gives its word by these rules when the letter is taken from the word (whither with two ticks = white, Italy with two = ity, crisis with three = cri, put with one = pt); the place of each mark under its group was not measured. (Corrected by the claims review of the same day: at 1359 and 800 the tick stands under another figure than the word needs, so all but those two marked groups come out by the printed rules.)

The three transcriptions collated into one file of 1,201 groups (we028.py). Of the eight value edits proposed on PR #900, six are applied in the collated file (628, 458, 845, 1081, 1564, 880): each has the blind film check, the sheet value and the clerk's uncorrected word for it, and was looked at on the frame. Two are not applied: 1257 on p. 5 (the three ticks under the group and the sheet want 1057, crisis less three letters; the digit is not settled on the frame; written 1057?) and 1388 on p. 18 (written over; 1383? kept). The code line missing from Dudout's p. 18 files is in the collated file. The contributors' files were not edited. Frames 0112-0115 and 0119-0121 looked at by an AI agent that knew the candidates; not blind, and no person has looked.

The readings compared place by place with the sheet and the clerk's decipherment. WAINUT's and Dudout's readings of pp. 17-18 differ in two words and both are settled: 70 is necessary (the clerk wrote 'ity' above it), 125 contrary. The sheet gives most of Dudout's values from the alphabetical slot and from sense and 12 of his 16 open groups (79 nevertheless, blu-e, ed-uc-ation, pass, name, monarch, alty, tal, observe); it shows ten of his values from sense to be slips or omissions of the writer (625, 1596, 1407, 1401, 1355, 797, 483, 1525, 1593, 545). On frame 0111 the clerk has 'en', 'over thro' and 'best' (his misreading of 1228 good) where Beling's transcription of the decipherment has enable, overthrow and best.

everett1825_collated_reading.md, the six parts as sentences against the code sheet: 844 cipher words, 23 holes, 0.973 (MS pp. 1-6: 573 of 587, 0.976; MS pp. 14-18: 248 of 257, 0.965; every MS page 0.956 or more). The holes are slips and omissions of the writer (a wrong group, a figure left out, a syllable or word with no group) and one group written over. Five words are read under the one-digit rule (1593, 1601, 1057 or 1257, 797, 1525). Thirteen words whose code spelling differs from the ordinary spelling by a letter are counted as read, as in ../jqa; as holes they would give 0.957, with part 6 at 0.946. The earlier per-page figures (0.904 for passages A to C, 0.917 to 0.949 for pp. 1, 2, 3 and 6) were counts against the rebuilt table and its overlay.

Reading review by a second AI agent that had not made the reading: every '> ' line read as sentences, and every line of the six parts checked against the decryption by eye and by a letter comparison: grade A, no group left out. It found two unmarked changes (the groups give 'refinement education' and 'prime Minister of Spain and Europe') and two unequal standards, and asked for four changes, all made: refine[d] and Minister[s] marked as holes (22 to 23 holes with for{+tune} moved the other way), the doubt on 1057 carried in the transcription, the one-digit rule applied to 797 as to the other slips.

Claims review of the page by a further AI agent, read-only: own decoder against the key file and the decryption (1,201 of 1,201 groups with the four sheet corrections), own word count, collation against the three transcriptions, and a look at the NARA frames (an AI model that knew the candidates, not blind). Verdict: the class holds. It found that the tick under 1359 stands under the 3 and the tick under 800 under the first 0, which by the printed rule withdraw i and u where describing and industrious want r and o; that 'the' in 'the correct principles' (114R.03.6, 1385 or 1345, film check split) was counted as read while [than] (1383 or 1388) was a hole; that the clerk's decipherment was used at nine places, not eight; and that the page called WAINUT and Brice Dudout the first decipherers although the clerk had deciphered all six passages at the time.

The claims review applied (maintainers' decisions): [the], des{+cri}b[i]ng and ind[u]strious marked as holes in everett1825_collated_reading.md. Recount (python we028.py count, and the reviewer's counter): 844 cipher words, 26 holes, 818 read, 0.969; MS pp. 1-6 570 of 587 (0.971), MS pp. 14-18 248 of 257 (0.965), MS p. 5 the lowest page at 0.954. The class depends on counting 17 words as read under the README rules for spellings and one-digit slips (13 spellings, 4 slips): as holes the whole would be 801 of 844 (0.949). The part split of 23 Nov 2026 (pp. 1-6 read from existing decipherment), decided before the code sheet was applied, withdrawn: outcome.parts removed, one method (read with known key) for all six parts; the clerk's decipherment stays the first decipherment.

texts.label: Everett, Notes of a conversation with Mr Zea, Madrid, 25 Sep 1825: the six coded parts (M31 reel 27 frames 0112-0115, 0119-0121)
texts.summary: Everett's private portrait of Francisco Zea Bermúdez, the Spanish minister whom he calls the prime Minister, and his reading of the refusal to recognise the new American states. Zea's frankness is real or assumed, and he said things he could not believe himself; he came into the cabinet through Ugarte, a creature of Russia, then sent him off on a mission to Turin; he is able, hard-working, liberal in conversation, less Spanish in manner than any Spaniard Everett has met. The foreign ministers think him privately well disposed to recognition but unable to risk his place against his rivals; the influence of the Emperor Alexander is against it, from a spirit of opposition to England rather than a regard for legitimacy.

The share depends on counting 17 words as read under the README rules for spellings and one-digit slips (13 spellings, 4 slips); as holes it would be 801 of 844, 0.949.
